title: Discrete 3D curve sampling, transported frames and absolute-time followers

supportedProfile: Bundle 0.3 curve program version1, three typed scalar coordinate expressions over a finite one-dimensional parameter domain
Fixed parameter samples, normalized cumulative chord-length lookup, explicit up/quaternion seed and discrete shortest-rotation parallel transport
Explicit total twist and preserve/distribute closed-seam policies; native GPU line strips plus mesh/group followers and native TeX anchors
Immutable line resources and deterministic source-time/parameter evaluation shared by the web and lecture consumers
excluded: General Blender curve types, Geometry Nodes graphs, spline evaluation or Blender output equivalence
Analytical arc-length integration, Frenet frames, between-sample singularity detection and arbitrary self-intersection guarantees
Tubes, profile sweeps, ribbons, surface generation and continuous differential-geometric certificates
Screen-space wide lines, dashed lines, line lighting, and identical raster bytes across GPU/browser implementations

upstream.role: Sample Curve motivates a normalized total-length query with separately sampled tangent data; Texloom uses its explicitly documented sampled chord-length policy.

mathematicalReferences.title: Parallel Transport Approach to Curve Framing
mathematicalReferences.publication: Indiana University Computer Science technical report 425 (1995)
mathematicalReferences.role: Discrete frame transport and cumulative-length distribution of closed-curve angular mismatch inform the explicit policies. Quaternion interpolation is used between sampled frames. This is an independent implementation and does not claim the report's complete tube or graphics pipeline.

inputs: Explicit operation/resource IDs, unit/m/cm/mm units, finite increasing domain and integer segments
Dimensionless u, time in seconds and typed scene parameters; scalar1 coordinate expressions interpreted in operation.units
An up seed not parallel to the first sampled tangent, or a quaternion with +X aligned to that tangent; optional total radians of twist
Followers reference a curve node and a mesh/group with the same parent. Curve local transform must be identity. Progress is dimensionless within[0,1]
At most16 operations,8192 segments per curve,32768 total segments and256 followers
outputs: Generated curve3d resources live in sampled frame.resources; authored packages retain only declarative operations and ordinary resources
frame.curves3d retains sampled positions, cumulative lengths, vertex tangents, orientation frames, reports and per-follower samples
Followers replace local translation/rotation, retain local scale and move native TeX children through the common evaluated3D hierarchy
Original TeX JSON bodies and decoded position/progress expressions have exact archived generated-source spans
coordinates: Curve resources are object-local right-handed XYZ in explicit units; GPU projection and node/ancestor transforms follow numerical sampling
Frame +X=tangent,+Y=normal,+Z=binormal; orientation is a unit quaternion
Position travels linearly along sampled chords. Orientation interpolates neighboring quaternions; its tangent can differ from the active chordTangent
Closed seam preserve retains transport holonomy; distribute corrects angular mismatch by cumulative length before applying explicit twist
errorPolicy: Reject nonfinite outputs, zero-length chords, reversing/cusp configurations without an unambiguous frame, invalid seeds and resource/unit conflicts
Closed endpoints must meet declared closureTolerance; accepted endpoints are made exactly identical
No clamping of invalid progress or silent conversion of distance/parameter values into normalized progress
Strict JSON capture rejects duplicate keys, nonfinite literals, unsafe paths, oversized captures, reserved metadata and duplicate resource/operation IDs
Follower target transform tracks conflict with derived translation/rotation and are diagnosed

verification.command: python -m unittest tests.curve3d_port_spec_test tests.curve3d_capture_test tests.curve_frames_player_test -v; npm test
claims: Real TeX captures the helix and follower program without authored line vertices, alongside a shared native arrow mesh and CM Bright labels
Browser tests independently calculate helix vertex/chord positions, verify right-handed orthonormal axes and project native label anchors
Reverse seeks match exact PNGs in the same browser; a radius control regenerates the curve while preserving the static arrow resource
Curve-only GPU scenes do not require dummy mesh triangles; nested fixture registration avoids rewriting historical2D golden images
notEstablished: Blender execution or equivalence to its evaluated splines, frame algorithms or full test corpus
Exact analytical arc length, curvature-normal construction or undetected between-sample degeneracies
Global frame continuity at undeclared cusps or all possible floating-point extremes
